title: OTLP stable-ingress compatibility hub with per-tenant mapping and adaptive ack
creator: Marcus Li
description: Build a lightweight OTLP "compatibility hub" that sits at the ingest boundary and performs tolerant schema translation, per-tenant mapping to backend exporters (Tempo/Jaeger), and an adaptive ack/backoff protocol to avoid head-of-line blocking during backend partial outages. This hub should make it easier to onboard new customers with non-standard OTLP variants, reduce dropped spans during backend pressure, and provide a documented runbook for adding new exporter backends.
acceptance_criteria: Hub can accept OTLP/gRPC and OTLP/http from at least three different client SDK variants and normalize them to a canonical span envelope
Per-tenant routing table used by hub maps tenant IDs to exporter sets (tempo-primary, jaeger-legacy, archive-s3) configurable via Console and stored in config-service
Adaptive ack/backoff: when target exporter signals high latency or 5xxs, hub switches to buffered async mode for that tenant and exposes metric 'hub.tenant.<id>.buffer_mode' = true
End-to-end test coverage with synthetic traces verifying ordering preservation, idempotency semantics for duplicate spans, and graceful failover to alternate exporter
Runbook published in Confluence with onboarding checklist and a GitHub PR template for adding backends
Dashboard panels added to Console: per-tenant ingest health, buffer occupancy, exporter latency percentiles, and synthetic trace pass rate
tasks: Design canonical span envelope and softening rules (allow unknown attributes, map common vendor fields)
Implement input adapters: otlp-grpc, otlp-http, and legacy jaeger thrift to OTLP translator
Build routing layer that reads per-tenant exporter config and supports atomic updates
Implement adaptive ack/backoff state machine with metrics and health probe integration
Integrate with existing exporter plugins for Tempo and Jaeger; add a generic batch-buffer sink for archive S3
Add e2e test harness using the trace-fuzzer (synthetic traces across 5 tenants) and golden trace comparator
Create Console dashboard tiles and wire up new metrics (buffer_size, ack_latency, exporter_5xx_rate)
Author onboarding runbook and exporter onboarding PR template; link to Confluence
Performance test: validate <2ms median extra latency for normal path at 10k rps and buffer failover under 5% token loss
Security review and KMS config check for tenant credential storage
comments: 2025-02-15 Marcus Li: Spiked a proto sketch and validated that two client variants (python-opentelemetry and mobile-sdk-v2) encode resource attributes differently. Proposal: implement field aliasing table and attribute fallback rules.

2025-02-18 Elena Rodriguez: Implemented initial otlp-http adapter and basic normalization. Found discrepancy: some SDKs set span.kind as string 'SERVER' vs enum. Normalizer should coerce case-insensitive strings to enums.

2025-02-20 Design review (Asha Patel): Prefer soft-skipping unknown attributes rather than failing ingestion. Add explicit header 'X-Hub-Compatibility-Mode' for debugging when we coerce or drop fields.
2025-02-22 Performance note (QA): Buffering mode tested with 50ms simulated exporter latency. Buffer occupancy increased predictably; need backpressure watermark at 75% to trigger eviction policy.
2025-02-26 Security (J. Morales): Tenant credentials should be stored in config-service with envelope encryption; confirm IAM roles for exporter access. Marked for security review.

2025-02-28 Elena Rodriguez: Merged initial routing layer into feature branch. Next: implement adaptive ack/backoff and Console metric plumbing. Planning to pair with SRE for load tests week of 2025-03-03.
